requirements.notes: The package is a thin IPC client; without a running terminal initialize() returns False and last_error() is (-6, 'Terminal: Authorization failed').

functions.name: initialize
functions.summary: Establish a connection with the MetaTrader 5 terminal.
signatures:
initialize(
   path,                     // path to the MetaTrader 5 terminal EXE file
   login=LOGIN,              // account number
   password="PASSWORD",      // password
   server="SERVER",          // server name as it is specified in the terminal
   timeout=TIMEOUT,          // timeout
   portable=False            // portable mode
   )

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: [in] Path to the metatrader.exe or metatrader64.exe file. Optional unnamed parameter. It is indicated first without a parameter name. If the path is not specified, the module attempts to find the executable file on its own.

parameters.name: login=LOGIN
parameters.description: [in] Trading account number. Optional named parameter. If not specified, the last trading account is used.

parameters.name: password="PASSWORD"
parameters.description: [in] Trading account password. Optional named parameter. If the password is not set, the password for a specified trading account saved in the terminal database is applied automatically.

parameters.name: server="SERVER"
parameters.description: [in] Trade server name. Optional named parameter. If the server is not set, the server for a specified trading account saved in the terminal database is applied automatically.

parameters.name: timeout=TIMEOUT
parameters.description: [in] Connection timeout in milliseconds. Optional named parameter. If not specified, the value of 60 000 (60 seconds) is applied.

parameters.name: portable=False
parameters.description: [in] Flag of the terminal launch in [portable](https://www.metatrader5.com/en/terminal/help/start_advanced/start#portable) mode. Optional named parameter. If not specified, the value of False is used.

functions.returns: Returns True in case of successful connection to the MetaTrader 5 terminal, otherwise - False.
notes: If required, the MetaTrader 5 terminal is launched to establish connection when executing the initialize() call.

functions.name: login
functions.summary: Connect to a trading account using specified parameters.
signatures:
login(
   login,                    // account number
   password="PASSWORD",      // password
   server="SERVER",          // server name as it is specified in the terminal
   timeout=TIMEOUT           // timeout
   )

parameters.name: login
parameters.description: [in] Trading account number. Required unnamed parameter.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: [in] Trading account password. Optional named parameter. If the password is not set, the password saved in the terminal database is applied automatically.

parameters.name: server
parameters.description: [in] Trade server name. Optional named parameter. If no server is set, the last used server is applied automatically.

parameters.name: timeout=TIMEOUT
parameters.description: [in] Connection timeout in milliseconds. Optional named parameter. If not specified, the value of 60 000 (60 seconds) is applied. If the connection is not established within the specified time, the call is forcibly terminated and the exception is generated.

functions.returns: True in case of a successful connection to the trade account, otherwise – False.

notes: The version() function returns the terminal version, build and release date as a tuple of three values:

notes: The function returns all data that can be obtained using [AccountInfoInteger](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/account/accountinfointeger), [AccountInfoDouble](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/account/accountinfodouble) and [AccountInfoString](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/account/accountinfostring) in one call.

notes: The function returns all data that can be obtained using [TerminalInfoInteger](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/check/terminalinfointeger), [TerminalInfoDouble](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/check/terminalinfodouble) and [TerminalInfoDouble](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/check/terminalinfodouble) in one call.

functions.name: symbols_total
functions.summary: Get the number of all financial instruments in the MetaTrader 5 terminal.
functions.returns: Integer value.
notes: The function is similar to [SymbolsTotal()](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/marketinformation/symbolstotal). However, it returns the number of all symbols including [custom](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/customsymbols) ones and the ones disabled in [MarketWatch](https://www.metatrader5.com/en/terminal/help/trading/market_watch).

functions.name: symbols_get
functions.summary: Get all financial instruments from the MetaTrader 5 terminal.

parameters.name: group="GROUP"
parameters.description: [in] The filter for arranging a group of necessary symbols. Optional parameter. If the group is specified, the function returns only symbols meeting a specified criteria.

functions.returns: Return symbols in the form of a tuple. Return None in case of an error. The info on the error can be obtained using [last_error()](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/python_metatrader5/mt5lasterror_py).
notes: The group parameter allows sorting out symbols by name. '*' can be used at the beginning and the end of a string.
The group parameter can be used as a named or an unnamed one. Both options work the same way. The named option (group="GROUP") makes the code easier to read.

The group parameter may contain several comma separated conditions. A condition can be set as a mask using '*'. The logical negation symbol '!' can be used for an exclusion. All conditions are applied sequentially, which means conditions of including to a group should be specified first followed by an exclusion condition. For example, group="*, !EUR" means that all symbols should be selected first and the ones containing "EUR" in their names should be excluded afterwards.
Unlike [symbol_info()](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/python_metatrader5/mt5symbolinfo_py), the symbols_get() function returns data on all requested symbols within a single call.

notes: The function returns all data that can be obtained using [SymbolInfoInteger](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/marketinformation/symbolinfointeger), [SymbolInfoDouble](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/marketinformation/symbolinfodouble) and [SymbolInfoString](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/marketinformation/symbolinfostring) in one call.

functions.name: copy_rates_from
functions.summary: Get bars from the MetaTrader 5 terminal starting from the specified date.
signatures:
copy_rates_from(
   symbol,       // symbol name
   timeframe,    // timeframe
   date_from,    // initial bar open date
   count         // number of bars
   )

parameters.name: symbol
parameters.description: [in] Financial instrument name, for example, "EURUSD". Required unnamed parameter.

parameters.name: timeframe
parameters.description: [in] Timeframe the bars are requested for. Set by a value from the [TIMEFRAME](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/python_metatrader5/mt5copyratesfrom_py#timeframe) enumeration. Required unnamed parameter.

parameters.name: date_from
parameters.description: [in] Date of opening of the first bar from the requested sample. Set by the 'datetime' object or as a number of seconds elapsed since 1970.01.01. Required unnamed parameter.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: [in] Number of bars to receive. Required unnamed parameter.

functions.returns: Returns bars as the numpy array with the named time, open, high, low, close, tick_volume, spread and real_volume columns. Return None in case of an error. The info on the error can be obtained using [last_error()](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/python_metatrader5/mt5lasterror_py).
notes: See the [CopyRates()](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/series/copyrates) function for more information.
Only data whose date is less than (earlier) or equal to the date specified will be returned. It means, the open time of any bar is always less or equal to the specified one.

MetaTrader 5 terminal provides bars only within a history available to a user on charts. The number of bars available to users is set in the "[Max. bars in chart](https://www.metatrader5.com/en/terminal/help/startworking/settings#max_bars)" parameter.

When creating the 'datetime' object, Python uses the local time zone, while MetaTrader 5 stores tick and bar open time in UTC time zone (without the shift). Therefore, 'datetime' should be created in UTC time for executing functions that use time. Data received from the MetaTrader 5 terminal has UTC time.
TIMEFRAME is an enumeration with possible chart period values

notes: See the [CopyRates()](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/series/copyrates) function for more information.

MetaTrader 5 terminal provides bars only within a history available to a user on charts. The number of bars available to users is set in the "[Max. bars in chart](https://www.metatrader5.com/en/terminal/help/startworking/settings#max_bars)" parameter.

copy_rates_range(

   )

parameters.name: symbol
parameters.description: [in] Financial instrument name, for example, "EURUSD". Required unnamed parameter.

parameters.name: timeframe
parameters.description: [in] Timeframe the bars are requested for. Set by a value from the [TIMEFRAME](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/python_metatrader5/mt5copyratesfrom_py#timeframe) enumeration. Required unnamed parameter.

parameters.name: date_from
parameters.description: [in] Date the bars are requested from. Set by the 'datetime' object or as a number of seconds elapsed since 1970.01.01. Bars with the open time >= date_from are returned. Required unnamed parameter.

parameters.name: date_to
parameters.description: [in] Date, up to which the bars are requested. Set by the 'datetime' object or as a number of seconds elapsed since 1970.01.01. Bars with the open time <= date_to are returned. Required unnamed parameter.

functions.returns: Returns bars as the numpy array with the named time, open, high, low, close, tick_volume, spread and real_volume columns. Returns None in case of an error. The info on the error can be obtained using [last_error()](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/python_metatrader5/mt5lasterror_py).
notes: See the [CopyRates()](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/series/copyrates) function for more information.

MetaTrader 5 terminal provides bars only within a history available to a user on charts. The number of bars available to users is set in the "[Max. bars in chart](https://www.metatrader5.com/en/terminal/help/startworking/settings#max_bars)" parameter.

When creating the 'datetime' object, Python uses the local time zone, while MetaTrader 5 stores tick and bar open time in UTC time zone (without the shift). Therefore, 'datetime' should be created in UTC time for executing functions that use time. Data received from the MetaTrader 5 terminal has UTC time.

functions.name: copy_ticks_from
functions.summary: Get ticks from the MetaTrader 5 terminal starting from the specified date.
signatures:
copy_ticks_from(
   symbol,       // symbol name
   date_from,    // date the ticks are requested from
   count,        // number of requested ticks
   flags         // combination of flags defining the type of requested ticks
   )

parameters.name: symbol
parameters.description: [in] Financial instrument name, for example, "EURUSD". Required unnamed parameter.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: [in] Date the ticks are requested from. Set by the 'datetime' object or as a number of seconds elapsed since 1970.01.01. Required unnamed parameter.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: [in] Number of ticks to receive. Required unnamed parameter.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: [in] A flag to define the type of the requested ticks. COPY_TICKS_INFO – ticks with Bid and/or Ask changes, COPY_TICKS_TRADE – ticks with changes in Last and Volume, COPY_TICKS_ALL – all ticks. Flag values are described in the [COPY_TICKS](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/python_metatrader5/mt5copyticksfrom_py#copy_ticks) enumeration. Required unnamed parameter.

functions.returns: Returns ticks as the numpy array with the named time, bid, ask, last and flags columns. The 'flags' value can be a combination of flags from the [TICK_FLAG](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/python_metatrader5/mt5copyticksfrom_py#tick_flag) enumeration. Return None in case of an error. The info on the error can be obtained using [last_error()](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/python_metatrader5/mt5lasterror_py).
notes: See the [CopyTicks](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/series/copyticks) function for more information.

When creating the 'datetime' object, Python uses the local time zone, while MetaTrader 5 stores tick and bar open time in UTC time zone (without the shift). Therefore, 'datetime' should be created in UTC time for executing functions that use time. Data received from the MetaTrader 5 terminal has UTC time.

COPY_TICKS defines the types of ticks that can be requested using the [copy_ticks_from()](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/python_metatrader5/mt5copyticksfrom_py) and [copy_ticks_range()](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/python_metatrader5/mt5copyticksrange_py) functions.

TICK_FLAG defines possible flags for ticks. These flags are used to describe ticks obtained by the [copy_ticks_from()](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/python_metatrader5/mt5copyticksfrom_py) and [copy_ticks_range()](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/python_metatrader5/mt5copyticksrange_py) functions.

COPY_TICKS_INFO – ticks with Bid and/or Ask changes, COPY_TICKS_TRADE – ticks with changes in Last and Volume, COPY_TICKS_ALL – all ticks. Flag values are described in the [COPY_TICKS](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/python_metatrader5/mt5copyticksfrom_py#copy_ticks) enumeration. Required unnamed parameter.

functions.returns: Returns ticks as the numpy array with the named time, bid, ask, last and flags columns. The 'flags' value can be a combination of flags from the [TICK_FLAG](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/python_metatrader5/mt5copyticksfrom_py#tick_flag) enumeration. Return None in case of an error. The info on the error can be obtained using [last_error()](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/python_metatrader5/mt5lasterror_py).
notes: See the [CopyTicks](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/series/copyticks) function for more information.

When creating the 'datetime' object, Python uses the local time zone, while MetaTrader 5 stores tick and bar open time in UTC time zone (without the shift). Therefore, 'datetime' should be created in UTC time for executing functions that use time. The data obtained from MetaTrader 5 have UTC time, but Python applies the local time shift again when trying to print them. Thus, the obtained data should also be corrected for visual presentation.

| --- | --- |
| action | Trading operation type. The value can be one of the values of the [TRADE_REQUEST_ACTIONS](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/python_metatrader5/mt5ordercheck_py#trade_request_actions) enumeration |
| magic | EA ID. Allows arranging the analytical handling of trading orders. Each EA can set a unique ID when sending a trading request |
| order | Order ticket. Required for modifying pending orders |
| symbol | The name of the trading instrument, for which the order is placed. Not required when modifying orders and closing positions |
| volume | Requested volume of a deal in lots. A real volume when making a deal depends on an [order execution type](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/python_metatrader5/mt5ordercheck_py#order_type_filling). |
| price | Price at which an order should be executed. The price is not set in case of market orders for instruments of the "Market Execution" ([SYMBOL_TRADE_EXECUTION_MARKET](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/constants/environment_state/marketinfoconstants#enum_symbol_trade_execution)) type having the [TRADE_ACTION_DEAL](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/python_metatrader5/mt5ordercheck_py#trade_request_actions) type |
| stoplimit | A price a pending Limit order is set at when the price reaches the 'price' value (this condition is mandatory). The pending order is not passed to the trading system until that moment |
| sl | A price a Stop Loss order is activated at when the price moves in an unfavorable direction |
| tp | A price a Take Profit order is activated at when the price moves in a favorable direction |
| deviation | Maximum acceptable deviation from the requested price, specified in [points](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/predefined/_point) |
| type | Order type. The value can be one of the values of the [ORDER_TYPE](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/python_metatrader5/mt5ordercalcmargin_py#order_type) enumeration |
| type_filling | Order filling type. The value can be one of the [ORDER_TYPE_FILLING](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/python_metatrader5/mt5ordercheck_py#order_type_filling) values |
| type_time | Order type by expiration. The value can be one of the [ORDER_TYPE_TIME](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/python_metatrader5/mt5ordercheck_py#order_type_time) values |
| expiration | Pending order expiration time (for [TIME_SPECIFIED](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/python_metatrader5/mt5ordercheck_py#order_type_time) type orders) |
| comment | Comment to an order |
| position | Position ticket. Fill it when changing and closing a position for its clear identification. Usually, it is the same as the ticket of the order that opened the position. |
| position_by | Opposite position ticket. It is used when closing a position by an opposite one (opened at the same symbol but in the opposite direction). |
notes: A trading request passes several verification stages on the trade server. First, the validity of all the necessary request fields is checked. If there are no errors, the server accepts the order for further handling. See the [OrderSend](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/trading/ordersend) function description for the details about executing trading operations.

functions.name: positions_total
functions.summary: Get the number of open positions.
functions.returns: Integer value.
notes: The function is similar to [PositionsTotal](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/trading/positionstotal).

functions.name: positions_get
functions.summary: Get open positions with the ability to filter by symbol or ticket.

parameters.name: symbol="SYMBOL"
parameters.description: [in] Symbol name. Optional named parameter. If a symbol is specified, the ticket parameter is ignored.

parameters.name: group="GROUP"
parameters.description: [in] The filter for arranging a group of necessary symbols. Optional named parameter. If the group is specified, the function returns only positions meeting a specified criteria for a symbol name.

parameters.name: ticket=TICKET
parameters.description: [in] Position ticket ([POSITION_TICKET](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/constants/tradingconstants/positionproperties#enum_position_property_integer)). Optional named parameter.

functions.returns: Return info in the form of a named tuple structure (namedtuple). Return None in case of an error. The info on the error can be obtained using [last_error()](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/python_metatrader5/mt5lasterror_py).
notes: The function allows receiving all open positions within one call similar to the [PositionsTotal](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/trading/positionstotal) and [PositionSelect](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/trading/positionselect) tandem.

The group parameter may contain several comma separated conditions. A condition can be set as a mask using '*'. The logical negation symbol '!' can be used for an exclusion. All conditions are applied sequentially, which means conditions of including to a group should be specified first followed by an exclusion condition. For example, group="*, !EUR" means that positions for all symbols should be selected first and the ones containing "EUR" in symbol names should be excluded afterwards.

COPY_TICKS_INFO.description: ticks containing Bid and/or Ask price changes

COPY_TICKS_TRADE.description: ticks containing Last and/or Volume price changes

ORDER_FILLING_FOK.description: This execution policy means that an order can be executed only in the specified volume. If the necessary amount of a financial instrument is currently unavailable in the market, the order will not be executed. The desired volume can be made up of several available offers.

ORDER_FILLING_IOC.description: An agreement to execute a deal at the maximum volume available in the market within the volume specified in the order. If the request cannot be filled completely, an order with the available volume will be executed, and the remaining volume will be canceled.

ORDER_FILLING_RETURN.description:
This policy is used only for market (ORDER_TYPE_BUY and ORDER_TYPE_SELL), limit and stop limit orders (ORDER_TYPE_BUY_LIMIT, ORDER_TYPE_SELL_LIMIT, ORDER_TYPE_BUY_STOP_LIMIT and ORDER_TYPE_SELL_STOP_LIMIT) and only for the symbols with Market or Exchange execution [modes](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/constants/environment_state/marketinfoconstants#enum_symbol_trade_execution). If filled partially, a market or limit order with the remaining volume is not canceled, and is processed further.
During activation of the ORDER_TYPE_BUY_STOP_LIMIT and ORDER_TYPE_SELL_STOP_LIMIT orders, an appropriate limit order ORDER_TYPE_BUY_LIMIT/ORDER_TYPE_SELL_LIMIT with the ORDER_FILLING_RETURN type is created.

ORDER_TIME_DAY.description: The order is active only during the current trading day

ORDER_TIME_GTC.description: The order stays in the queue until it is manually canceled

ORDER_TIME_SPECIFIED.description: The order is active until the specified date

ORDER_TIME_SPECIFIED_DAY.description: The order is active until 23:59:59 of the specified day. If this time appears to be out of a trading session, the expiration is processed at the nearest trading time.

ORDER_TYPE_BUY_STOP_LIMIT.description: Upon reaching the order price, Buy Limit pending order is placed at StopLimit price

ORDER_TYPE_CLOSE_BY.description: Order for closing a position by an opposite one

ORDER_TYPE_SELL_STOP_LIMIT.description: Upon reaching the order price, Sell Limit pending order is placed at StopLimit price

TRADE_ACTION_CLOSE_BY.description: Close a position by an opposite one

TRADE_ACTION_DEAL.description: Place an order for an instant deal with the specified parameters (set a market order)

TRADE_ACTION_MODIFY.description: Change parameters of the previously placed trading order

TRADE_ACTION_PENDING.description: Place an order for performing a deal at specified conditions (pending order)

TRADE_ACTION_SLTP.description: Change open position Stop Loss and Take Profit

measured_notes.history_deals_get: **Measured calling convention.** The range form needs **both** dates and only as positional arguments: `history_deals_get(since, now)`. A single date, a third positional argument, or keyword arguments all return `None` with `last_error() == (-2, 'Invalid arguments')`. The single-record form uses the keyword filter: `history_deals_get(ticket=...)` or `history_deals_get(position=...)`.
measured_notes.history_orders_get: **Measured calling convention.** Same as `history_deals_get`: `history_orders_get(since, now)` positionally, or `history_orders_get(ticket=...)` as a keyword filter.
measured_notes.history_deals_total: **Measured calling convention.** `history_deals_total(since, now)` - two positional dates. With no arguments it returns `None` with `(-2, 'Invalid arguments')`; with keyword arguments it raises `TypeError`.
measured_notes.history_orders_total: **Measured calling convention.** `history_orders_total(since, now)` - two positional dates. With no arguments it returns `None` with `(-2, 'Invalid arguments')`; with keyword arguments it raises `TypeError`.
measured_notes.order_check: **Measured.** `order_check` has its own retcode: `0` with comment `'Done'` means the request is acceptable. Only then are `balance`, `equity`, `margin`, `margin_free` and `margin_level` populated. It does **not** use the `TRADE_RETCODE_*` family.
measured_notes.order_send: **Measured.** Success is `retcode == mt5.TRADE_RETCODE_DONE` (10009) with comment `'Request executed'`. `bid` and `ask` stay `0.0` in the answer; the fill price is in `price`. The `request` field echoes the structure the terminal received.
measured_notes.symbol_info: **Measured.** `filling_mode` is a bitmask (1=FOK, 2=IOC, 4=RETURN) and the package does not export `SYMBOL_FILLING_*`, so map it yourself before choosing `type_filling`. A mismatch is rejected with retcode `10030`.
measured_notes.copy_ticks_from: **Measured.** Returns `None` when the account has no tick history for the requested window - that is not an error, it means the feed has no ticks there.
measured_notes.positions_get: **Measured.** Returns a tuple of `TradePosition`; an empty tuple when there are no open positions. `None` means the call itself failed - check `last_error()`.
